messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING SRE oncall — Canary warmup skew detected for model redwood-v13 in us-west1. p99 streaming tail latency spiked to ~12.3s (baseline ~0.6s). Auto-page to oncall. Please assemble in #incidents and join the bridge if needed.

pagerduty: Auto-pager: paging @devin (oncall). Incident priority: P1.

devin: I'm oncall, joining bridge now. starting quick check of metrics and canary weights.

maria: Observability: KV cache miss rate for redwood-v13 nodes jumped at canary start, mux queue depth increased ~x6. p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~12.3s for streaming endpoints. Logs show frequent kv_load timeouts around the same window.

sunita: probable warmup/priming imbalance — new model variant has larger KV size + cold prefix patterns. streaming path isn't warming fast enough under traffic shift.

jon: Can we immediate-reduce canary weight to limit blast radius? I can run the rollout CLI.

devin: yes. reducing canary weight to 1% now. executing:
```
# reduce canary weight
redwood rollout set --model redwood-v13 --canary-weight 1
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout weight update accepted. canary weight changed from 10 -> 1. triggered config push to us-west1.

maria: after weight drop: p99 trending down to ~3.4s (2m after change). still above SLO but improving. streaming stalls reduced but some long sessions still show retries.

devin: rolling full rollback to stable v12 on the canary fleet while we triage.
```
# rollback to previous stable variant
redwood rollout rollback --model redwood-v13 --target v12-stable --confirm
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for redwood-v13 canary nodes. ETA ~ 3-5 minutes to converge.

maria: Notifying CS: low-level customer impact seen for multi-minute streaming sessions started during the canary window. No bulk errors, just degraded latency and a handful of stalls. CS, please triage accounts with active sessions around T0.

cs-lead: Acknowledged, pulling sessions and contacting top-5 impacted customers. drafting communication.

devin: collecting traces and kv cache histograms. grabbing pprof and streaming trace snippets now. Also dumping model KV sizes for comparison.

sunita: quick mitigation idea: enable prefix prefetch for the canary variant or fallback to quantized kernels that reduce initial KV footprints. But we need a safe longer-term fix — model onboarding checklist missing warmup ramp.

devin: enabled streaming fallback routing to stable path for in-flight sessions. command:
```
# enable fallback routing for streaming mux
redwood routing set --route streaming --fallback stable-path --duration 10m
```

maria: after rollback + fallback: p99 back to 0.85s, p95 ~0.45s. trend looks normal at last check. marking as mitigated but will keep monitoring for 30m.

jon: created temporary alert rule to catch KV miss-rate regressions specifically for canary variants. will add to playbook.

devin: collected heap + trace artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/5419876543/artifacts.tar.gz. (traces + kv histograms + pprof).

sunita: adding follow-up actions: 1) onboarding checklist update (warmup profile + priming traffic), 2) automated warmup job for large-KV models, 3) canary weight ramp automation with KV warmup gating.

maria: CS sent initial outreach to impacted customers, flagging transient latency and that we rolled canary back. No escalations so far.

oncall: Keeping bridge open for 30m post-mitigation. If no regressions, we'll close and start postmortem doc.

devin: confirm p99 stable at 0.78s 10m after rollback. closing live paging but keeping notes. I'll create triage doc and assign to ML/Infra.

maria: thanks everyone. tagging SRE, ML, Infra for postmortem: @devin @sunita @jon @maria.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated. follow-up: create postmortem and link artifacts.

maria: will file postmortem and include customer impact summary.

devin: leaving final action items in the triage doc and linking runbooks. Bridge clear in 15.

oncall: closing thread once artifacts attached. good job team. :thumbsup:
